results.question: Summarize the three laboratory experiments covered by this report.
results.answer:
The report covers three laboratory experiments conducted during the spring semester, all assembled on solderless breadboards and verified with a mixed-signal oscilloscope [Blocks 1-12]:

- **Lab 04 – 4-to-1 multiplexer:** Implemented with the 74HC153 integrated circuit, it selects one of four data inputs and routes it to a single output under the control of two select lines, S1 and S0. It was verified with an exhaustive truth table test across all sixteen select-and-data combinations, with a typical propagation delay of 14 nanoseconds [Blocks 1-12].
- **Lab 05 – Inverting operational amplifier:** Built around a TL072 op-amp with a 10 kilo-ohm input resistor and a 100 kilo-ohm feedback resistor. The measured voltage gain was -9.8, within 2 percent of the ideal -10, and the measured -3 decibel bandwidth was 48 kilohertz [Blocks 1-12].
- **Lab 06 – 4-bit synchronous counter:** Used the 74LS163 integrated circuit clocked at 1 kilohertz, advancing through all sixteen states from 0000 to 1111 without skipped or stuck states, with correct ripple carry cascading behavior. A fault appeared when the clear line was asserted for fewer than 20 nanoseconds, confirming the datasheet minimum pulse width requirement [Blocks 1-12].

All three circuits met their design targets, with limitations noted regarding breadboard contact resistance and room-temperature-only counter testing [Blocks 13-15].
